newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee softer on trade demand for dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee softer on trade demand for dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee weakened in early Wednesday trade due to commercial demand for the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT the rupee was quoted at 58.58 to the dollar, after opening at 58.54 and moving to 58.65, they said. The rupee closed at 58.52 on Tuesday.
"The rupee, which is falling on import covering, could easily go to about 58.70 to the dollar by the end of the day," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were also low with the market being very well offered, dealers said.
"Overnight call has been at 9.25 percent, despite a big state bank borrowing heavily," said a Union Bank dealer.
Overnight call money closed on Tuesday at 9.25 percent.
